title: A task says which failing walk it owns instead of being guessed at
goal: When the walk sweep lists its failures, it now says which of them another open task is already working on. It works that out by looking for the walk name anywhere in the other task, so a task that mentions a walk only in passing can be listed as owning it, and a runner can skip a walk nobody is actually fixing. Make that a thing a task says about itself rather than something guessed from its text.
notes: Added by a-sweep-result-stops-wiping-what-a-person-wrote on 2026-09-13. ownersOfWalks in queue/bin/sweep-notes.mjs joins title, goal, notes and acceptance and does a substring match on the walk name. Real example from the 20:35Z sweep: dock-picked-first-walk came out owned by two tasks, picking-a-plain-shape-leaves-the-panel-parked-on and picking-a-text-layer-leaves-its-settings-below-t, and only the first is really about it. A declared field (walks: ["..."]) on the task, with the text match kept as a fallback, is the obvious shape.
acceptance: A task can name the walks it owns in a way the sweep reads directly, and the sweep prefers that over matching text
A walk named only in passing in another task is not listed as owned by it
The existing tasks that really do own a failing walk are updated to say so
queue/bin/sweep-notes-drill.mjs covers both cases and passes

log.note: TRIAGE 2026-09-14, seen live: the sweep block in walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep currently reads "dock-picked-first-walk -> picking-a-plain-shape-leaves-the-panel-parked-on, picking-a-text-layer-leaves-its-settings-below-t, a-task-says-which-failing-walk-it-owns-instead-o". This task is listed as an owner of that walk purely because its goal uses the walk name as an example. That is exactly the failure it describes, and it means a runner reading the block can decide a real failure belongs to somebody else.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building. The obvious shape (a walks field, text match kept as a fallback) is half a fix on its own: the real 20:35Z example had ONE task claiming dock-picked-first-walk correctly and two claiming it from a passing mention, and a per-walk 'declared beats guessed' rule only helps the walks somebody remembered to claim. So the rule is also per TASK: a task that has declared is taken at its word and its prose is not read at all, which gives a task about the walk machinery a way to stop claiming its own examples (walks: [] means 'I own none of them'). That is what made this task's own false claim on dock-picked-first-walk fixable rather than only illustrative. Rejected as decoration: validating claims against the walk library on every sweep (a walk about to be written is fair to claim in advance), and a second opinion where a guess is listed alongside a claim (the point is to stop the guess, not to rank it).

Built. queue/bin/sweep-notes.mjs: walkName, declaredWalks, and ownersOfWalks now returning { ids, declared } per walk; machineBlock labels each ownership line as claimed or guessed and, when any line is a guess, prints the command that ends it. queue-lib.mjs: normalizeWalks, setWalks, and a walks option on addTask (absent and empty mean different things, so an empty array is stored rather than dropped). queue.mjs: 'walks <id> [<walk> ... | --none]', printing what the task has said when given no walks and warning about a name with no walk file behind it. dashboard.html: a 'Walks it owns' fact on the task dialog.

Verified. sweep-notes-drill.mjs is now 48 checks (was 25) and all pass; the new ones crash against the old code, proved by stashing the three source files and re-running. Every other drill green: failure-drill 90 checks, leftovers (2 scenarios), manager-due 14, decision, churn, audit-index, state-poll. Scripts/test.sh: 8083 tests in 643 suites, passed. Recomputed over the LIVE queue and the real 115-walk failing list: turn-into-a-path-walk is no longer claimed by a-hundred-and-fifteen-walks-fail-on-code-that-pa (it was, from a passing mention), and appearance-list-min, tutorial-mark-it-up-walk, size-limits-walk and first-run-walk now read as claimed. The dashboard row was read out of the live page at 127.0.0.1:8791 and photographed.

Live tasks updated to say what they own: a-hundred-and-fifteen-walks-fail-on-code-that-pa claims its four reproduction walks; an-audit-gets-a-real-picture-of-the-app-again says none (its walk is named only as a way to reproduce a capture failure); this task says none (dock-picked-first-walk is its example). The hand-written paragraph under the sweep block on walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep said ownership is always a text match, which is no longer true, so it now describes both.

LEFT ROUGH, none of it clearing the follow-up bar. (1) No real sweep has written the new block: the Mac has been locked since 2026-09-15 so every sweep since reports 'could not run', which is a-hundred-and-fifteen-walks-fail-on-code-that-pa's ground and not a new task. (2) On the task dialog four walk names wrap onto four lines in a narrow Facts column; it reads, but a long list will look cramped. (3) Nothing re-checks a claim after it is made: a task claiming a walk that is later renamed or deleted keeps the claim, and only the moment of claiming warns. Nobody is stopped by either of the last two, so they live here.
